..

Next 7 Days..

Ridging will continue to build into the Western CONUS over the 
next few days as an area of low pressure moves out of the four 
corners region into the southern plains. These higher heights will
allow for daytime highs to be above average through most of the 
next week. Some places Sunday could even push 70F. It does appear 
that record high temps are out of reach now though.

The most impactful weather this weekend is the potential for some
gusty winds in the western parts of our CWA. Two weak shortwaves 
will push through Montana (closer to the international border) 
Today and Tomorrow. These vort maxes will come with mainly dry 
conditions.

The first wave that moves along the international border Today 
will be much more impactful for areas to our NW but we will still 
see breezy winds. The REFS is showing 700mb winds of 20 to 30kts 
across the CWA midday which is roughly in line with what the long 
range models have been showing for the past few days. The wind 
direction looks to be slightly north of west which could limit 
some of the gap influence along the Big Timber to Harlowton 
corridor. Wind gusts in this area could reach 40 mph during the 
day today with even lower values for Billings and points east. 
That being said, gusts in the 40 mph range have already been 
observed early this morning, but this is likely due to winds 
ducting below the nocturnal inversion. 

The second wave will move into NW MT during the day Sunday before
pushing into central AB. As of the latest model runs, it looks 
like this wave will bring us stronger winds aloft. Stronger winds 
from the Big Timber to Harlowton region are anticipated with this 
feature for two reasons. The first being that the winds at the 
700mb layer will be a little higher (around 40kts according to the
REFS) and the wind direction will be due westerly. This could be 
conducive for gusts in the 50s mph along US-191 Sunday afternoon. 
The rest of the region could see wind gusts in the 30s mph for 
much of the day. This will be something to keep an eye on though 
as if this wave does push a little more south or east then we 
could be talking about a more widespread event with stronger 
winds. 

The strongest, and most impactful, winds this weekend look to be 
a result of the gap flow out of the Paradise Valley. The GFS/GEFS 
are both showing pressure gradient values fron IDA to LWT of 
10-14mb before sunrise both this morning and Sunday morning. It is
worth noting that the observed gradient is already sitting around
the higher end of that range at the time of writing this. The 
inversion tonight has setup pretty well with minimal cloud cover 
and conditions are expected to be quite similar 24 hours from now.
The gap flow this morning will remain relatively limited due to 
the weaker winds aloft though. That being said, the pressure 
gradient and inversion alone should allow for winds to continue 
gusting in the 40s mph over the next few hours. Sunday AM, with a 
near identical MSLP and temperature setup, does look to be more 
conducive for some stronger gusts though. As the next shortwave 
advects into the Northern Rockies, winds aloft will pick up pretty
quickly. As mentioned above, the REFS is showing 40 kts at 700mb 
which, combined with the other ingredients, will be sufficient to 
see gusts over 50mph. Additionally, the farther south you go, the 
winds will have more of a southerly component which could further 
enhance the strong wind potential. Due to all of this, the 
decision was made to not issue any wind products with the main 
forecast package, however obs will be closely monitored through 
the morning hours. The need for any products Sunday AM will be 
reevaluated later today.
 
In addition to the gap winds Sunday AM, there is also a signal 
for some weak downslope / mountain wave activity near Red Lodge. 
Winds at the Beartooths' ridgetop are forecast to increase through
the morning hours Sunday before peaking at 30-40kts around 
sunrise. The GFS shows a good area of subsidence on the lee side 
of the terrain (near Red Lodge) all the way from the surface up to
500mb. Due to the wind speeds aloft, there likely will not be 
overly impressive wind speeds at the surface, however some windy 
conditions around sunrise Sunday are certainly possible in the 
foothills near Red Lodge and Absarokee. 

Looking ahead to next week, it appears that the overall pattern 
for our region remains relatively quiet. Long range models do show
more weak short waves pass near the our CWA but none of which 
seem to be more impactful than some breezy winds or a few showers.
Looking out towards the middle of the month though, both the GEFS
and ECMWF Ensembles show a more progressive pattern with temps 
closer to average. WMR
